run_2_k32769.note: The tracked script takes K through --ks, so no copy was made and no tracked file was edited. fp32 at K=32769 was skipped: the GPU budget was already used up (about 17 min total against the 15 min box).

comparison_to_published.published: 3.52 (docs/findings.md:512, Oct 4); 3.59 on 2.14.1 and 3.62 on nightly (docs/upstream/pytorch-mps-wide-linear-issue.md:61, Oct 9); README.md:33 says 3.6x

_environment: torch 2.14.1 (repo .venv), macOS 27.0.1, Apple M1 Max (32 GB), MPS available. Runs serialized through bench/with_gpu.sh (flock on /tmp/mac-kernels-gpu.lock). Host state before the run: load averages 14.08 / 21.95 / 21.43, uptime 3 days 23 h, swap used 631.5 MB of 2048 MB, no pmset thermal or performance warning recorded; top CPU users were mds_stores (79%), Arc browser helpers (31% and 25%), WindowServer (30%). Default run 2026-11-09 10:24:58 to 10:35:07 PST (about 10 min); K=32768/32769 fp16 run 10:35:19 to 10:41:53 PST (about 6.5 min). Total GPU time about 17 min, 2 min over the 15 min box. Script settings were the defaults: M=4608, N=6144, min ms over 3 interleaved rounds x 5 iterations after warm-up.
_interpretation:
1. The transposed-weight slowdown still reproduces today on torch 2.14.1: at K=32768 F.linear is 3.23x slower than the contiguous pre-transposed matmul in fp16 and 7.89x in fp32, with identical outputs (max abs diff 0). That is a little under the published 3.52x/3.59x fp16 and 8.41x-8.83x fp32 (docs/findings.md:512; docs/upstream/pytorch-mps-wide-linear-issue.md:61, :65; README.md:33). The absolute slow-path times are nearly unchanged (684 vs 714.6 ms fp16, 2103 vs 2067.7 ms fp32); the ratio dropped because the contiguous fast path measured slower today (211 vs 199 ms fp16, 266 vs 246 ms fp32), consistent with the host load average of 14-22 during the run. The K=16384 ratios (1.90 fp16, 4.30 fp32) match the published 1.91 and 4.24-4.42 (pytorch-mps-wide-linear-issue.md:59, :64).
2. The slowdown does not depend on K being a power of two. It grows smoothly with K across every non-power-of-two value in the default sweep (fp16: 1.17x at 8192, 1.26x at 10240, 1.33x at 12288, 2.16x at 24576; fp32: 2.52x, 2.70x, 3.05x, 6.87x at the same Ks), and the transposed-left-operand variant stays near the contiguous one throughout, as the issue text says (pytorch-mps-wide-linear-issue.md:25).
3. K=32769 is a different regime, not a test of the same effect: every variant, including the contiguous one, jumps to about 2.3 s (contiguous 210.8 ms at 32768 vs 2268.7 ms at 32769, a 10.8x cliff), so the ratio collapses to 1.05 only because everything is slow. This is the K > 32768 correctness reroute on M1/M2 that the script docstring (bench/repro_mps_wide_linear.py:3-4) and the issue draft (pytorch-mps-wide-linear-issue.md:9, :44) warn about. For the PyTorch issue, a K=32769 row should be labeled as the reroute path rather than presented as evidence either way about the transposed-weight bug. fp32 at K=32769 was not run (GPU budget). No repo files were edited; raw logs are in the scratchpad paths listed in table_json.
